data.title: How a Tunnel Under a River Works

sentences.text: If you dig a shaft and a hole under a river, you have a tunnel.
But the soft mud caves in, and river water floods the hole.
So you push a steel shield forward that holds the mud back.
Behind it, you line the walls with rings of concrete segments.
This is a tunnel boring machine.
Its wheel spins and cuts, and a belt carries the mud out.
But now the long, closed tunnel fills with smoky air.
So you add big fans that push in fresh air.
In the Holland Tunnel, 84 fans change all its air every 90 seconds.
Add a road and lights along the ceiling.
Congratulations, you have built a tunnel under a river.
